DRUGS (LABELLING AND PACKING) RULES, 1986
DRUGS
(LABELLING AND PACKING) RULES, 1986
(Amendments)
[Gazette
of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part II,
30th September, 2010
S.R.O. 918(I)/2010, dated 30-9-2010.---In
exercise of the powers conferred by section 43 of the Drugs Act, 1976 (XXXI of
1976), the Federal Government is pleased to make following further amendments
in the Drugs (Labelling and Packing) Rules, 1986, the same having been previously published as
required by subsection (3) of the said section, namely:--
In the aforesaid rules,---
(1) in rule 2, after clause (a), the
following new clause shall be inserted, namely:--
(aa) medical device means a disposable
syringe, disposable set for collection or transfusion of blood or giving any
infusion, canula, catheter, stent, auto-disable syringe or butterfly needle; ;
(2)
after rule 14, the following new rules shall be added, namely:---
15.
Labelling for medical devices.---The label of a medical device in
addition to the particulars required to be given under rule 3, bear the
following particulars in a conspicuous manner, namely:--
(i) The
nominal capacity;
(ii) type
of nozzle,---
(a)
integrated needle;
(b)
non-integrated needle;
(c)
fixed needle;
(d)
slip tip needle; or
(e)
leur lock needle;
(iii) needdle
size and dimension;
(iv) Sterile ;
(v) For
Single Use Only ;
(vi) auto
disable symbol in case of auto disable syringes;
(vii) a
warning to check the integrity of primary container for example Do not use if
blister is punctured or not intact ;
(viii) information for handling, storage and
disposal of syringe on secondary container;
(ix) type
of syringe in case of insulin syringe; and
(x) units
of activity like U -40 or U-100 in case of insulin syringe.
16. Manner
of packing of disposable syringes.---The disposable syringes shall be packed
only in blister packing and not in polyethylene packing. The packing materials
used will be such that, if gas sterilization method is applied, it permits easy
permeation of gases across it and does not affect sterility throughout its
shelf life.. .
